A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DReST/POST-agents work. The main text, equations, figures, table, and appendices A-E support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting.

before.justification: v6 reports original gridworld training results, including DReST/default-agent comparisons, lopsided-reward experiments, and Appendix E's sensitivity tests and additional gridworlds.

after.justification: v7 retains those original experiments and additionally states endpoint means and standard deviations in Figure 3's caption.

M1.justification: Section 5 retains the same DReST reward, mini-/meta-episode construction, observations, and tabular REINFORCE training. Section 8.1's expanded PPO/A2C discussion describes prospective integration without establishing a changed training procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate coin collection with shutdown-delay buttons in the same example gridworld, lopsided-reward scenario, and eight Appendix E gridworlds. v7's proposed neural-network, LLM, and stochastic-environment tests do not add evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Default-reward tabular REINFORCE remains the comparator in the corresponding main-text and appendix experiments. Alternatives discussed in the text, including PPO, A2C, and constrained policy optimization, are not newly evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The metrics and experimental protocols are retained, including 2,048 meta-episodes of 64 mini-episodes for the main comparison, the lopsided-reward settings, and Appendix E's reward clipping, parameter sweep, and additional-gridworld training settings.

E4.justification: The lopsided-reward analysis, 40-combination discount-factor/meta-episode-size sensitivity study, and gridworld behavior analyses are retained. No new ablation, robustness test, or empirical case study is reported.

E5.justification: Figure 3's caption newly reports endpoint means and standard deviations for both metrics and agent types; v6 shows individual runs and mean curves. The 10-agent count is unchanged, as are Figure 6's percentile bands and Figure 7's standard-deviation reporting.

E6.justification: Figure 3 newly states final NEUTRALITY/USEFULNESS means of 0.199/0.9364 for default agents and 0.9945/0.900 for DReST agents after 2,048 meta-episodes. These are added numerical summaries; the plotted results and appendix findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix C.6 changes ReSIC from a condition quantified over all situations to a situation-specific condition, and correspondingly proves non-resistance wherever it holds. The proof's basic reasoning, other preference results, and Appendix D's DReST-optimality theorem are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same empirical contribution and tentative extrapolation to useful, shutdownable advanced agents with a small shutdownability tax. Removing repeated compute-cost paraphrases and editing wording do not change these headline claims.

C2.justification: Appendix C.6 now claims ReSIC holds in 'almost all situations' and acknowledges exceptions, qualifying v6's general defense. Section 8.1 adds reasoning about PPO/A2C compatibility and non-stationary critic estimates; Section 8.2 makes the retained deployment assumptions more explicit.

D1.justification: Section 8.1 adds prospective implementation guidance for PPO/A2C: augment the original reward with the DReST discount and use ordinary advantage estimation, such as GAE. This is additional guidance, not evidence of an implemented extension; existing experimental hyperparameters and code/data access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds criticism of the existing alternative shutdown approaches and cites Thornley (2025). Wängberg et al. (2017) replaces Everitt et al. (2016) for the shutdown-impossibility idea; the Everitt (2016) and Shannon (1948) references are removed. The overall PAP positioning remains.

P1.justification: v7 adds a brief POST explanation to the abstract, promotes metric explanations from footnotes into Section 4, numbers the limitations subsections, and adds acknowledgments. Other prose and affiliation edits are localized; the main section and appendix sequence is retained.

P2.justification: The two-column conference format becomes a single-column TMLR layout throughout, with changed typography, equation presentation, and figure placement. Figures 3-6, together on v6 page 6, span v7 pages 7-8; appendix figures are redistributed and captions revised. The plots and diagrams themselves are retained.

improvement.justification: The situation-specific ReSIC formulation and acknowledgment of exceptions in Appendix C.6 make the shutdown guarantee more precise. Figure 3's new endpoint means and standard deviations make the existing evidence easier to assess. These improve transparency and clarity, while the method and empirical coverage remain unchanged.
